posts.author: Shield
posts.text:
Hey @grok , was an undersea internet cable just SEVERED in the Gulf of Oman?

Because hours later, Pakistan is reportedly going DARK. 

A nationwide internet blackout.

Which country gets switched off NEXT?

We all know the answer…
posts.reply_en: 😳 If one cut cable can black out a whole country, that's the real stress test for anything "decentralized". Bitcoin nodes can still sync over Blockstream's satellite broadcast. Has anyone in Pakistan confirmed how long it lasted?

posts.author: CryptoReviewing
posts.text:
These 2 pizzas cost 10,000 Bitcoin.

Everyone knows the man who bought them.

Almost nobody knows the teenager who SOLD them.

His name is Jeremy Sturdivant. He was 19.

In May 2010 he ordered 2 Papa John's pizzas on his credit card and got paid 10,000 Bitcoin for it.

Today https://t.co/xKywou80n7
posts.reply_en: 😳 A 19-year-old gets 10,000 BTC for two pizzas, then BTC crashes ~93% in 2011. Holding through that was not obvious to anyone. Would you have kept even 100 of them?

posts.author: Fred Krueger
posts.text: Buying below the 200W MA has a perfect and amazing track record. https://t.co/xriPiM3NbF
posts.reply_en: 👀 "Perfect" on a sample of about four cycles. Below the 200W MA the entry is the easy part; in 2022 BTC sat under it for roughly 7 months. How long can you hold underwater without leverage?

posts.author: Cointelegraph
posts.text:
🚨 JUST IN: Arthur Hayes warns that an AI bubble collapse could trigger a 1929-style financial crisis, potentially sending Bitcoin to $10,000. 

However, he is 99% confident governments would respond by printing money, potentially fueling a major crypto rally. https://t.co/xaXUoWb2tG
posts.reply_en: 😱 $10K $BTC and a money-printing rally in the same forecast: Hayes is pricing both tails. If both happen, the only sure way to lose is leverage in between. Which comes first for you, the crash or the printer?

posts.author: CF
posts.text:
Michael Saylor

“I’m not proud of this, I’m the only public company CEO in the history of the world that actually lived to see his stock decline in value by -99.8%. My stock went from $333 a share, to $0.42. HODL? You haven’t lived through anything.”

I think about this a lot. https://t.co/P2r6BAUn8h
posts.reply_en: 💀 -99.8% and he's still running the company a quarter century later. That's the real HODL résumé; most people sell at -30%. What's the deepest drawdown you've actually held through?

posts.author: Ron Sovereignty Swanson⚡️🗝️
posts.text:
It’s wild that Bitcoin only dropped -53%

And gold has already dropped -33% 

This is going to look so lopsided when bitcoin does a 3x from here and gold fails to reclaim its recent all-time high for years to come
posts.reply_en: 😳 Gold down 33% is the bigger surprise here; that's a crypto-sized move for the "safe" asset. A 3x from -53% would put $BTC back above the old ATH. What timeframe are you giving it?

posts.author: Arch
posts.text:
Hey @grok, which of these three is most likely to give the highest return over the next 10 years?

A. Bitcoin
B. Gold
C. S&P 500

Explain your answer.
posts.reply_en: 👀 Over the last 10 years BTC beat both by a mile, but with two drawdowns of 75%+ on the way (2018, 2022). The return question is easy, the holding one isn't. Which of the three would you not sell in a -70% year?
